title: serve() documents a 0600 socket but creates it with the process umask and chmods afterwards, leaving a connectable window
description:
persona-grpc/src/server.rs:370-393. The doc comment promises "Creates parent directories if needed. Sets socket permissions to 0600." The implementation binds first and fixes permissions second:

    let listener = UnixListener::bind(socket_path)?;        // line 387
    ...
    std::fs::set_permissions(socket_path, Permissions::from_mode(0o600))?;   // line 392

bind() creates the socket inode with 0777 & ~umask, so between line 387 and line 392 the mode is whatever the daemon umask yields. Connecting to a Unix socket requires write permission, so the exposure depends on umask:
  • umask 022 (systemd default) -> 0755: others cannot connect. Not exploitable.
  • umask 002 (common on distros using per-user groups, and on many developer shells) -> 0775: any member of the users primary group can connect during the window.
  • umask 000 -> 0777: any local user can connect.

Given that no consumer attestation runs on the issuance path (filed separately), a connection that lands inside that window gets a full JWT-SVID for the users identity.

The same ordering issue applies to the parent directory: create_dir_all at server.rs:383-385 creates /run/user/{uid}/persona with 0777 & ~umask rather than 0700. On the default personad path this is contained, because systemd creates /run/user/{uid} itself as 0700 -- but serve() is a public function taking an arbitrary path, and it is already called with a /tmp path by persona-grpc/tests/e2e.rs:236, where no such containment exists.

Why this belongs in the tree rather than being ignored: the function states a guarantee it does not provide, and the guarantee is the only thing standing between an unauthenticated local caller and the users identity. A contributor reading the doc comment will not re-derive the umask interaction. Note also that the ordering at server.rs:378-385 removes a stale socket before ensuring the parent directory exists, which is harmless but backwards.

Fix direction: set umask to 0177 around the bind and restore it, or bind into a directory created 0700 first and rely on directory permissions; either way make the doc comment describe what is actually enforced.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.92 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
